title.ja: Step Functions: 状態機械、retry と catch、Map、待ち合わせ、saga
title.en: Step Functions: State Machines, Retry and Catch, Map, Callbacks, and Sagas

sources.title: Choosing workflow type in Step Functions
supports: The workflow type cannot be changed after a state machine is created

Standard: up to one year, exactly-once workflow execution unless Retry is specified in ASL, execution state persisted between state transitions, history retrievable through the API for 90 days after completion, billed by state transition

Express: up to five minutes, billed by number of executions, duration and memory; asynchronous Express is at-least-once, synchronous Express is at-most-once; execution state is not persisted between transitions and history is not captured by Step Functions
Express Workflows do not support the .sync and .waitForTaskToken integration patterns, Distributed Map, or activities
For Standard, starting an execution with the name of a running one returns an idempotent response; for Express, the same name results in concurrent executions
StartSyncExecution from the console expires after 60 seconds

sources.title: Transforming data with JSONata in Step Functions
supports: Step Functions implements JSONata based on the 2.0.6 specification; $eval is not available, $parse replaces it
When creating a workflow in the console, AWS recommends JSONata as the top-level QueryLanguage; without the field the default is JSONPath
JSONata states use Arguments and Output in place of InputPath, Parameters, ResultSelector, ResultPath and OutputPath, and a string is an expression only when it starts with {% and ends with %}
$states holds input, result, errorOutput (in a Catch) and context
An expression that returns no value, a type error, an evaluation longer than one second, and exceeded memory all raise States.QueryEvaluationError, which Retry and Catch can name
Step Functions adds $partition, $range, $hash, $random, $uuid and $parse
A Choice rule in JSONata has a Condition

sources.title: Passing data between states with variables
supports: Assign is available on Pass, Task, Map, Parallel, Choice and Wait states, and inside Catch and Choice rules
All expressions in an Assign are evaluated with the values on state entry, then assigned; the new values are visible from the next state
Assign and Output are processed in parallel
A variable is at most 256 KiB, all variables in one Assign at most 256 KiB together, and all stored variables at most 10 MiB per execution
Parallel branches and Map iterations read outer variables and keep their own; a Distributed Map cannot reference outer variables

sources.title: Amazon States Language (specification)
supports: In JSONata states a Catcher may have Output and Assign, which may reference $states.errorOutput; without Output the state output is the Error Output, an object with Error and usually Cause
When a state reports an error, the matching Catcher's Assign is evaluated and the state's top-level Assign is not
ItemSelector overrides each item of a Map; $states.context.Map.Item.Value and .Index describe the item
A MaxConcurrency of 1 processes the items in order
sources.note: The specification states the default of a missing Output twice and differently: "the result in a Task, Map, and Parallel State" in the section on Arguments and Output, and "the Task State copies its input through to its output" in the section on the Task state. The chapter's definitions write Output in every Task and Map so that neither reading matters.

sources.title: Discover service integration patterns in Step Functions
supports: Three patterns: Request Response, Run a Job (.sync), Wait for a Callback with Task Token (.waitForTaskToken), chosen by the suffix of Resource
AWS SDK integrations: Request Response in Standard and Express, .waitForTaskToken in Standard, no .sync
Optimized DynamoDB supports Request Response only; SQS, SNS and Lambda support Request Response and, in Standard, the callback; Step Functions, ECS, and others support .sync
A task waiting for a token waits until the execution reaches one year unless HeartbeatSeconds or TimeoutSeconds is set
If a task using a callback token times out, a new random token is generated
Task tokens must be returned by principals in the same account
A .sync task that is aborted is cancelled on a best-effort basis; .sync polling consumes API quota

sources.title: Handling errors in Step Functions workflows
supports: Retrier fields and defaults: IntervalSeconds 1, MaxAttempts 3 (0 never retries), BackoffRate 2.0, MaxDelaySeconds, JitterStrategy FULL or NONE (default NONE; FULL randomizes each interval between 0 and its computed value)
A retrier's counters apply across all visits to it within one state execution (the page's complex retry scenario: ErrorA, ErrorB, ErrorC, ErrorB)
States.ALL matches every known error name except States.Runtime and States.DataLimitExceeded, must be alone and last; States.TaskFailed matches every error except States.Timeout
Retries are treated as state transitions
Catchers exist for Task, Parallel and Map states, not for the execution as a whole
The page lists States.HeartbeatTimeout as the error of a missed heartbeat

sources.title: Task workflow state
supports: TimeoutSeconds and HeartbeatSeconds both default to 99,999,999; HeartbeatSeconds must be smaller than TimeoutSeconds
The page says a missed heartbeat fails the task with States.Timeout
The optimized Lambda integration is arn:aws:states:::lambda:invoke; a function ARN as Resource is the legacy form
Arguments and Output are the JSONata fields of a Task
sources.note: Two pages name the error of a missed heartbeat differently (States.Timeout here and on the integration patterns page, States.HeartbeatTimeout on the error handling page). The chapter's Retry names both.

sources.title: Learning to use AWS service SDK integrations in Step Functions
supports: The Resource of an SDK integration is arn:aws:states:::aws-sdk:serviceName:apiAction, with parameters in PascalCase

The error name of an SDK integration is ServiceName.ErrorName with the suffix Exception added even when the service's own name lacks it (S3.BucketAlreadyExistsException); the exception prefix of Amazon S3 is S3
Step Functions cannot generate IAM policies for SDK integrations

sources.title: Perform DynamoDB CRUD operations with Step Functions
supports: The optimized integration offers GetItem, PutItem, UpdateItem and DeleteItem, Request Response only
Errors of the optimized integration carry the prefix DynamoDB; the SDK integration uses DynamoDb
The IAM policy for static resources names the table ARN

sources.title: Send messages to an Amazon SQS queue with Step Functions
supports: arn:aws:states:::sqs:sendMessage.waitForTaskToken with the token from $states.context.Task.Token in a MessageBody object
The role needs sqs:SendMessage on the queue

sources.title: Publish messages to an Amazon SNS topic with Step Functions
supports: arn:aws:states:::sns:publish with TopicArn, Message and MessageAttributes
The role needs sns:Publish on the topic

sources.title: Map workflow state
supports: Inline mode: up to 40 concurrent iterations, a JSON array as input, iterations recorded in the parent's history

Distributed mode: each iteration a child workflow execution, up to 10,000 in parallel, input from a JSON array or S3; for datasets over 256 KiB, histories over 25,000 events, or more than 40 concurrent iterations

sources.title: Using Map state in Inline mode in Step Functions workflows
supports: In inline mode the failure of any iteration fails the Map state and stops all iterations
MaxConcurrency 0 places no limit; 1 processes items in order; the output is an array of the iterations' outputs
Items is the JSONata field for the array; ItemProcessor replaces Iterator

sources.title: Using Map state in Distributed mode for large-scale parallel workloads
supports: Distributed mode is supported in Standard workflows only; ExecutionType of the child workflows is STANDARD or EXPRESS
ToleratedFailurePercentage and ToleratedFailureCount set how many failed items a Map Run tolerates before it fails
A Retry on a Distributed Map applies to the whole Map Run and creates a new one

sources.title: Choice workflow state
supports: A JSONata Choice rule has a Condition; Default is optional and recommended

sources.title: Parallel workflow state
supports: Branches are state machines run in parallel; the state has Arguments, Output, Assign, Retry and Catch

sources.title: Wait workflow state
supports: Seconds or Timestamp; the longest wait is one year in Standard and five minutes in Express

sources.title: Step Functions service quotas
supports: 256 KiB of UTF-8 for the input or output of a task, state, or execution, in both types
25,000 events in a Standard execution's history; unlimited in Express
Maximum execution time one year (Standard) and five minutes (Express)
Redrivable period 14 days; redrive is not supported for Express

Outside us-east-1, us-west-2 and eu-west-1: StartExecution bucket 800 with 150 refilled per second for Standard, 6,000 and 6,000 for Express; StateTransition bucket 800, refill 800 for Standard, unlimited for Express
1,000 published versions and 100 aliases per state machine
Up to 10,000 parallel child executions in a Map Run

sources.title: Restarting state machine executions with redrive in Step Functions
supports: A redrive continues from the unsuccessful step with the same input and the same definition, even if an alias now points elsewhere
A redriven Task state is scheduled again and its retry count reset; a Fail state is re-entered and fails again
An inline Map redrives only the iterations that failed
Redrives count as state transitions
The caller needs states:RedriveExecution on the execution ARN

sources.title: State machine versions in Step Functions workflows
supports: A version is a numbered, immutable snapshot with the ARN <state machine ARN>:<number>
Definition, role, tracing and logging configuration belong to a version

sources.title: State machine aliases in Step Functions workflows
supports: An alias points to one or two versions of the same state machine and can route traffic between them

sources.title: UpdateStateMachine
supports: Running executions continue to use the previous definition and role
Executions started immediately after the call may still use the previous definition

sources.title: StartExecution
supports: Idempotent for Standard: the same name and input as a running execution returns the same response; a closed execution or a different input returns ExecutionAlreadyExists; a name can be reused 90 days after the execution closes
Not idempotent for Express
An unqualified state machine ARN uses the latest revision; a version or alias ARN starts that version

sources.title: StartSyncExecution
supports: Only for Express; answers 200 even when the execution fails, with the status in the body
The response carries billingDetails with billedDurationInMilliseconds and billedMemoryUsedInMB

sources.title: SendTaskSuccess
supports: Reports that the task identified by taskToken completed, with output as a JSON string of at most 262,144 bytes
Errors include TaskTimedOut: the task token has either expired or the task associated with the token has already been closed

sources.title: SendTaskHeartbeat
supports: Resets the heartbeat clock of the task that owns the token

sources.title: Testing state machines with TestState API
supports: Since November 2025 TestState accepts a mock for the service integration, a full definition with stateName, a context, and a state configuration such as the retry count
With a mock the role is optional and no service is called
status is SUCCEEDED, FAILED, RETRIABLE or CAUGHT_ERROR, and nextState names the next state
Mocked results are validated against the service's API model unless fieldValidationMode is relaxed
Testing a Map state tests its input and output processing, not the ItemProcessor
The console's test feature does not support mocks yet

sources.title: TestState
supports: Request fields: definition, stateName, input, mock, context, stateConfiguration, variables, roleArn, inspectionLevel
A mock may be given only for Task, Map and Parallel states, and a context only together with a mock

sources.title: Testing state machines with Step Functions Local (unsupported)
supports: Step Functions Local does not provide feature parity and is unsupported; AWS points to the TestState API instead

sources.title: Using CloudWatch Logs to log execution history in Step Functions
supports: Express workflows record no history in Step Functions; logging to CloudWatch Logs must be configured to see one, and delivery is best effort
Logs are billed at the vended logs rate
The execution role needs the ten logs actions of the example policy on Resource *, because those actions accept no resource
Log levels ALL, ERROR, FATAL, OFF
Log group names prefixed /aws/vendedlogs/states keep the account's resource policy small

sources.title: Monitoring Step Functions metrics using Amazon CloudWatch
supports: The AWS/States namespace has ExecutionsFailed, ExecutionsTimedOut, ExecutionsAborted, ExecutionThrottled, ExecutionTime, and for Express ExpressExecutionMemory, ExpressExecutionBilledMemory and ExpressExecutionBilledDuration

sources.title: Automating Step Functions event delivery with EventBridge
supports: Only Standard workflows emit execution status change events to the default event bus

sources.title: Creating an IAM role for your state machine in Step Functions
supports: AWS recommends aws:SourceArn and aws:SourceAccount in the role's trust policy, with arn:aws:states:<region>:<account>:stateMachine:* as an example

sources.title: AWS Step Functions pricing
supports: Standard: charged per state transition, retries included; 4,000 transitions a month are free indefinitely
The page's first example counts four transitions for a workflow of two steps: Start, the two steps, End
Express: a request is counted each time a workflow starts; duration is rounded up to 100 ms and memory is billed in 64 MB chunks
Express memory is estimated as 50 MB plus the definition size plus the execution data size times the number of Map or Parallel steps

sources.title: AWS Price List: AmazonStates, ap-northeast-1
supports: Published 2026-09-11T12:45:11Z: USD 0.000025 per state transition; Express USD 0.000001 per request and USD 0.00001667 per GB-second for the first 3.6 million GB-seconds, then 0.00000833, then 0.00000456

sources.title: DeleteObject
supports: Deleting a key that does not exist returns 204

sources.title: CopyObject
supports: Copying within general purpose buckets needs s3:GetObject on the source object and s3:PutObject on the destination

sources.title: Reserved words in DynamoDB
supports: STATE and STATUS are reserved words, so an attribute by such a name needs an expression attribute name

sources.title: jsonata (npm registry metadata)
supports: The reference implementation of JSONata, MIT licensed, without dependencies; version 2.0.6 was published on 2024-11-29
Expression.evaluate(input, bindings) returns a promise and binds each key of bindings as a variable
sources.note: Read from the registry metadata and the installed package's jsonata.d.ts.

sources.title: cdkd v0.296.28: register-providers.ts
supports: cdkd 0.296.28 registers dedicated providers for AWS::DynamoDB::Table, AWS::IAM::Policy, AWS::IAM::Role, AWS::Logs::LogGroup, AWS::S3::Bucket, AWS::S3::BucketPolicy, AWS::SNS::Topic, AWS::SNS::TopicPolicy, AWS::SQS::Queue, AWS::SQS::QueuePolicy and AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
Its state machine provider passes DefinitionString, RoleArn, StateMachineType, LoggingConfiguration and TracingConfiguration to CreateStateMachine
It has no provider named for AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachineVersion or StateMachineAlias
sources.note: Confirmed in the dist of the installed package (@go-to-k/cdkd 0.296.28), not on GitHub.

sources.title: Cloudflare Workflows
supports: As of 2026-10-13: durable multi-step execution on Workers, written as code with step.do, with automatic retries, sleep, and step.waitForEvent to pause for external events; available on the Free and Paid plans

sources.title: Cloudflare Workflows: Sleeping and retrying
supports: As of 2026-10-13: a step takes retries (limit, delay, backoff) and a timeout; NonRetryableError stops retrying
A rollback handler can be attached to step.do for saga-style compensation; when the Workflow later fails, registered handlers run in reverse step-start order

sources.title: Vercel Workflows
supports: As of 2026-10-13: Vercel Workflows runs multi-step logic as durable code that can retry failed steps, wait for external events, and resume across crashes and deployments

definition.ja: いくつかのサービスにまたがる変更を、1 つのトランザクションにまとめる代わりに、ステップごとに確定させていくやり方。後のステップが失敗したら、済んだステップを補償処理で打ち消す。途中の状態は外から見える。
definition.en: A change that spans several services, made by committing one step at a time instead of in one transaction. When a later step fails, the steps already done are cancelled by compensations. The states in between are visible from outside.

definition.ja: Step Functions が、外からの返事を待つタスクに付ける文字列。返事をする側は、このトークンを添えて SendTaskSuccess か SendTaskFailure を呼ぶ。
definition.en: A string Step Functions attaches to a task that waits for an answer from outside. Whoever answers calls SendTaskSuccess or SendTaskFailure with it.

definition.ja: JSON を選んで組み替えるための式の言語。Step Functions のステートの中では、`{% %}` で囲んだ文字列が JSONata の式として評価される。
definition.en: An expression language for selecting and reshaping JSON. Inside a Step Functions state, a string wrapped in `{% %}` is evaluated as JSONata.

definition.ja: Step Functions のワークフローの種類の 1 つ。最長 5 分で、途中の状態を保存せず、実行の回数と時間とメモリで課金される。同じ実行が 2 回走ることがある。
definition.en: One of the two kinds of Step Functions workflow: five minutes at most, no state persisted between steps, billed by executions, duration and memory, and an execution may run twice.

definition.ja: 長くかかるタスクが「まだ動いている」と知らせる合図。HeartbeatSeconds の間に届かなければ、Step Functions はそのタスクを失敗にする。
definition.en: The signal by which a long task says it is still working. If none arrives within HeartbeatSeconds, Step Functions fails the task.

tiers.description: Express Workflows - Duration - USD 0.00001667 per GB-S for the first 3.6 million GB-Seconds
Express Workflows - Duration - USD 0.00000833 per GB-S for the next 14.4 million GB-Seconds
Express Workflows - Duration - USD 0.00000456 per GB-S above 18 million GB-Seconds

unknownAllowances.reason: The pricing page names a free tier for state transitions only. No free allowance for Express requests was found on it (read 2026-10-13).
The pricing page names a free tier for state transitions only. No free allowance for Express duration was found on it (read 2026-10-13).

title.ja: Step Functions: デプロイ済みで、1 回も実行しない月
title.en: Step Functions: deployed, and never started, for a month

ja: ステートマシン、テーブル（オンデマンド）、バケット、キュー、トピック、ロググループは、置いてあるだけでは課金されない
バケットにもテーブルにも何も入っていない
en: The state machines, the on-demand table, the bucket, the queue, the topic, and the log group cost nothing while they only exist
Neither the bucket nor the table holds anything

title.ja: Step Functions: 取り込みを月に 1,000 回（Standard、すべて成功）
title.en: Step Functions: 1,000 imports a month (Standard, all succeeding)

ja: 1 回の実行は CreateNote、AttachFile、WaitForScan、Verdict、Publish、Notify、Imported を 1 回ずつ通る。開始と終了を足して状態遷移は 9 と数える（料金ページの例の数え方。実測ではない）
再試行、補償処理、redrive は起きない。起きれば、そのぶん状態遷移が増える
DynamoDB の書き込みは PutItem と UpdateItem の 2 回で、アイテムは 1 KB 以下（1 回 1 unit）
S3 はアップロードの PUT と、取り込みの COPY が 1 回ずつ
SQS は、送信、受信、削除が 1 回ずつ。空の受信は数えていない
未算入: 添付ファイルの保存料金、通知の配送先ごとの料金、スキャンをする側の料金
en: One execution passes CreateNote, AttachFile, WaitForScan, Verdict, Publish, Notify and Imported once each. With start and end that is counted as 9 state transitions (the pricing page's way of counting; not measured)
No retries, compensations or redrives. Each one would add state transitions
Two DynamoDB writes, PutItem and UpdateItem, on an item of at most 1 KB (one unit each)
S3 sees one PUT for the upload and one COPY for the import
SQS sees one send, one receive and one delete. Empty receives are not counted
Not included: storage of the attachments, delivery charges of the notice per subscriber, whatever does the scanning

title.ja: Step Functions: 10 件の照会を月に 100,000 回（Express）
title.en: Step Functions: 100,000 lookups of 10 notes a month (Express)

ja: 1 回の実行は 10 件のノートを GetItem で読む。300 ミリ秒かかると仮定（計測した値ではない）
メモリは 64 MB として課金される（50 MB と、定義と入出力の大きさの合計が 64 MB に収まる）
GetItem は結果整合で、4 KB 以下のアイテムにつき 0.5 unit
ログは ERROR だけで、失敗は起きない。ログの取り込みは 0
en: One execution reads 10 notes with GetItem and is assumed to take 300 ms (not measured)
Billed at 64 MB of memory (50 MB plus the definition and the payloads stays within 64 MB)
GetItem is eventually consistent: 0.5 units for an item of at most 4 KB
Logging is at ERROR and nothing fails, so nothing is ingested

items.basis: 100,000 x 0.3 s x 0.0625 GB, in GB-seconds

title.ja: Step Functions: 同じ照会を Standard で動かしたとき
title.en: Step Functions: the same lookups as a Standard workflow

ja: 仕事は「10 件の照会を月に 100,000 回（Express）」と同じ
状態遷移は、Map が 1、10 回の GetNote が 10、開始と終了で 2、合わせて 13 と数える。Map の繰り返しがどう数えられるかは料金ページに書かれておらず、この数は見積もりで、実測ではない
Standard は実行の時間には課金されない
en: The same work as "100,000 lookups of 10 notes a month (Express)"

State transitions are counted as 13: one for the Map, ten for the ten GetNote states, two for start and end. The pricing page does not say how Map iterations are counted; this is an estimate, not a measurement
A Standard workflow is not billed for its duration

note.ja: テスト 66 件。手元の実行器（Retry の数え方と待ち時間、エラー名の一致、値のない式、Catch の出力、Assign の評価順、コールバックのトークン、Map）、取り込みの saga（各ステップの失敗と、応答だけが失われた場合、2 回走ったステップ、スキャンの拒否、Publish の先での失敗、補償処理の失敗と redrive、同じノート ID の 2 つの取り込み、わざと壊した定義 2 つ）、照会（公開前のノートを見せないこと、2 回走っても同じ答え）、TestState に送る表と実行器の一致、スタックのアサーション。相手はすべてメモリ上の代役で、Step Functions でも DynamoDB でも S3 でもない
note.en: 66 tests. The local interpreter (how retries are counted and how long they wait, error name matching, an expression with no value, a catcher's output, the evaluation order of Assign, callback tokens, Map), the import saga (each step failing and each step's answer getting lost, a step that runs twice, a refused scan, failures past Publish, a failing compensation and its redrive, two imports of one note ID, two definitions broken on purpose), the digest (a note not yet published stays hidden, the same answer when run twice), the table sent to TestState against the interpreter, and stack assertions. Everything ran against in-memory stand-ins: not Step Functions, DynamoDB, or S3
Type check of src, test, scripts, and infra

note.ja: 既定、`--infected --refuse RemoveAttachment --times 4 --redrive`、`--lose CreateNote` の 3 通りを実行し、通ったステート、残ったもの、不変条件の判定が本文の出力と同じであることを確かめた
note.en: Ran the default, `--infected --refuse RemoveAttachment --times 4 --redrive`, and `--lose CreateNote`, and checked that the states passed, what was left behind, and the invariant verdict are what the page shows

note.ja: AihStepFunctions のテンプレートが、AWS に問い合わせずに生成されること
note.en: The AihStepFunctions template is synthesized without asking AWS anything

records.command: vp run sfn:infra:deploy / sfn:start / sfn:callback / sfn:status / sfn:digest / sfn:empty / sfn:infra:destroy

note.ja: デプロイしていない。2 つのステートマシンは、AWS では一度も動かしていない
note.en: Not deployed. Neither state machine has ever run on AWS

note.ja: TestState API を呼んでいない（認証情報が要る）。手元の実行器と本物の Step Functions が同じ答えを出すかどうかは、確かめていない
note.en: The TestState API was not called (it needs credentials). Whether the local interpreter and the real Step Functions give the same answers has not been checked

summary.ja: 47章の手元の実行器は自作のモデルで、本物の Step Functions と突き合わせていない。未確認: JSONata の式（`$merge`、`&` での連結、`$exists`、`$count`、要素が 1 つの配列の扱い）を Step Functions が同じ値に評価すること。Retry と Catch の選び方、`MaxAttempts: 0` の retrier の扱い。`Output` を省いたときの既定（仕様書の 2 か所で記述が食い違う）。
summary.en: Chapter 47's local interpreter is a model of the author's own and has not been compared with the real Step Functions. Unconfirmed: that Step Functions evaluates the JSONata expressions (`$merge`, concatenation with `&`, `$exists`, `$count`, an array of one element) to the same values; how retriers and catchers are chosen, and how a retrier with `MaxAttempts: 0` behaves; the default of a missing `Output` (the specification says two different things in two places).

resume.ja: 認証情報を用意して `vp run sfn:test-state` を実行する。スタックは要らず、モックを使うので他のサービスは呼ばれない。`DIFFERENT` と出た行が、モデルの誤りか、表の誤り。直したら `vp test run examples/47-step-functions` で表と実行器が一致することを確かめる。
resume.en: With credentials, run `vp run sfn:test-state`. No stack is needed, and with mocks no other service is called. A line marked `DIFFERENT` is an error in the model or in the table. After fixing it, check with `vp test run examples/47-step-functions` that the table and the interpreter agree.

summary.ja: 47章のスタックを AWS に一度もデプロイしていない。未確認: cdkd 0.296.28 が、`Fn::Join` で組み立てた JSONata の `DefinitionString` と `LoggingConfiguration` つきの Express ステートマシンを作れること。ロールの信頼ポリシーの条件が通ること。各ステートの権限が足りること（特に、`aws-sdk:s3:copyObject` に `s3:GetObject` と `s3:PutObject` だけで足りるか）。DynamoDB の条件式が意図どおりに働くこと、エラー名が `DynamoDB.ConditionalCheckFailedException` であること。コピー元がないときのエラー名。`sqs:sendMessage.waitForTaskToken` が `MessageBody` のオブジェクトを JSON の文字列として送ること。ハートビートが途切れたときのエラー名（ドキュメントのページによって `States.Timeout` と `States.HeartbeatTimeout` に分かれる）。再試行で新しいトークンが配られること。redrive が補償処理のステートから再開すること。Express の実行時間と課金されるメモリ、状態遷移の実際の数（Map の繰り返しの数え方を含む）。
summary.en: The chapter 47 stack has never been deployed. Unconfirmed: that cdkd 0.296.28 creates a state machine from a JSONata `DefinitionString` assembled with `Fn::Join`, and an Express one with a `LoggingConfiguration`; that the trust policy conditions are accepted; that each state's permissions suffice (in particular whether `s3:GetObject` and `s3:PutObject` are enough for `aws-sdk:s3:copyObject`); that the DynamoDB condition expressions behave as intended and the error is named `DynamoDB.ConditionalCheckFailedException`; the error name when the copy source is missing; that `sqs:sendMessage.waitForTaskToken` sends an object `MessageBody` as a JSON string; the error name of a missed heartbeat (the documentation says `States.Timeout` on some pages and `States.HeartbeatTimeout` on another); that a retry is given a new token; that a redrive resumes from a compensation state; the duration and billed memory of the Express workflow, and the real number of state transitions, including how Map iterations are counted.

resume.ja: `vp run sfn:infra:deploy`、`vp run sfn:start`、`vp run sfn:callback --verdict clean`、`vp run sfn:status`、`vp run sfn:digest --ids note-1,nope` の順に実行する。失敗の経路は、別のノート ID で `sfn:start` し、`sfn:callback --verdict infected` で確かめる。補償処理の失敗は、実行中にロールから `s3:DeleteObject` を一時的に外して起こし、戻してから `vp run sfn:status --redrive <ARN>` で再開する。終わったら `vp run sfn:empty --yes` と `vp run sfn:infra:destroy`。
resume.en: Run `vp run sfn:infra:deploy`, `vp run sfn:start`, `vp run sfn:callback --verdict clean`, `vp run sfn:status`, and `vp run sfn:digest --ids note-1,nope`. For the failure path, start another note ID and answer `sfn:callback --verdict infected`. To make a compensation fail, remove `s3:DeleteObject` from the role for a while during a run, put it back, and resume with `vp run sfn:status --redrive <ARN>`. Finish with `vp run sfn:empty --yes` and `vp run sfn:infra:destroy`.
